name: Calliste Green
lede: Calliste Green is a strong yellow-green from a 1912 color plate, closest in our archive to the greens Georges Seurat and Paul Gauguin reached for.

sections.title: A plate from 1912, filed by Maerz and Paul
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary of color dates the name to 1912, at plate 19, column L, chip 6, hex #92A03F [1]. No Ridgway or ISCC-NBS citation is recorded for it in this library, so the dictionary entry is its only documented source [1]. Its Munsell renotation is 3.2GY 6.2/7.1, a strong, fairly saturated yellow-green [1]. The sources consulted here do not explain the name "Calliste," and its origin is undocumented [1].

The nearest library names are [[lettuce-green|Lettuce Green]], a duller, more olive green about 4.3 units away, and [[reseda|Reseda]], also duller, at 4.5 units [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within six units of Calliste Green covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 51 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.2 per cent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s decade, and three painters carry it far above the archive average: Niels Larsen Stevns, Georges Seurat and Paul Gauguin, each more than twenty-five times the base rate [2]. Its earliest appearance is a 1613 *Crucifixion* by Luis Tristán, where it covers only eight per cent of the canvas [2]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, read as screen colors [2].
